<section_guide number="1" title="Overview">
<purpose>Capture the target user and core problem, then the final business impact that should constrain every PoC proposal.</purpose>

<questions>
1. Who is the main target user, and what core problem should this PoC address?
2. What final business impact should that user gain, and why does it matter?
</questions>

<workflow>
Ask one question at a time, or both only when the user can answer them together easily. Integrate
the answer before asking for the next missing item.

Keep Section 1 to two inputs. Target User and Core Problem combines the main user and problem.
Desired Business Impact states the final outcome the user should gain and why it matters. Preserve
a measurement signal when the user already has one, but do not require a metric to complete the
Section.

Do not ask for a solution, screen, starting state, user-action sequence, demo procedure, detailed
current-alternative analysis, FAQ, architecture, or implementation plan. Use one short statement for
each input unless the user already supplied more detail.
</workflow>

<completion required="true">Confirm Target User and Core Problem and Desired Business Impact before saving 1.1-1.2 separately.</completion>
</section_guide>
